November 15, 2026

Trump blames Biden for nationwide ground stop as travel chaos continues

tags: politics, government
sources: @aaronparnas

More than 24 hours after a nationwide ground stop disrupted air travel, President Trump made his first public comments, attributing the failure to the Biden administration and calling the air traffic control system old and broken. He urged Congress to approve billions of dollars quickly for a new flight control system, saying the FAA is ready to proceed. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said on air that the administration would not apologize, placing responsibility on the previous administration. Flights continued to be cancelled, with roughly 1.5 million travellers reported stranded, while administration staff had earlier acknowledged that a system upgrade carried out on the Friday before Thanksgiving had crashed.

White House threatens criminal prosecution of Senator Elizabeth Warren

tags: politics, legal
sources: @aaronparnas

A US attorney in Texas sent Senator Elizabeth Warren a letter demanding she preserve documents related to her investigations of President Trump and of corporations that donate to him. White House chief of staff Stephen Miller reposted the letter alongside references to 18 U.S.C. 241 and 242, federal conspiracy statutes covering deprivation of rights under color of law. The citation was read as a threat to prosecute Warren over her oversight work. Legal commentary noted that the Constitution's speech or debate clause shields legislative functions, including investigations of the executive branch, from criminal prosecution.

Speaker Johnson blames Democrats for lack of FAA funding

tags: politics, government
sources: @aaronparnas

House Speaker Mike Johnson said Republicans were unable to secure Democratic support for additional FAA funding for Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy's department and had to proceed with Republican votes alone. Republicans currently hold the House, the Senate and the White House, and passed billions of dollars in funding for ICE and CBP personnel without Democratic votes. Democrats have said they supported increased funding for the Department of Transportation.

Trump administration continues rolling back airline passenger protections

tags: politics, markets
sources: @aaronparnas

Over the past 18 months the Trump administration has rolled back passenger rights rules covering cash compensation, wheelchair handling and hidden or junk fees, according to The New York Times. This year it abandoned a Biden-era rule that would have required airlines to disclose charges for extras, and the Department of Transportation reversed a 15-year-old requirement that airlines display the final ticket price more prominently. Penalties and fines against airlines have also been halted. The changes come as stranded travellers face surge pricing from ride-hailing and rental car companies.

Former Louisiana police officer sentenced to castration for child sex crimes

tags: legal, politics
sources: @aaronparnas

Cajun Williams, a 31-year-old former police officer in Louisiana, was sentenced to three life terms after convictions including first-degree rape and indecent behavior with a juvenile. As part of the punishment he is also to be castrated, under a 2024 Louisiana law that made the state the first in the nation to allow castration as a penalty for certain sex crimes. It is not yet clear whether the castration will be surgical or chemical, and the sentence is believed to be among the first applications of the law.

White House social accounts post AI-generated images of Trump

tags: politics, media
sources: @aaronparnas

The White House and President Trump's social media accounts have continued posting AI-generated imagery, including a picture depicting Trump behind bars and a sequence of fabricated images showing him in the Oval Office comforting Senator Markwayne Mullin's son. The images are not real. The posts appeared while roughly 1.5 million Americans were stranded by air travel disruptions and before the president had commented on the nationwide ground stop.
